member.name: T:DotnetClaw.Agents.ClawAgentLoop
member.summary:
The core agentic loop for DotnetClaw.
Architecture mirrors OpenClaw's tool-use loop: 1. Session starts → workspace identity documents are loaded and prepended to the system prompt (SOUL.md → AGENTS.md → USER.md → custom docs) 2. User sends a message 3. Agent decides which tools (plugins) to call 4. Tool results are fed back into context 5. Loop repeats until the agent produces a final text response OR the max-iteration guard fires
Uses Microsoft Semantic Kernel's as the agent runtime, with automatic function calling enabled.

member.name: T:DotnetClaw.Browser.BrowserSessionManager
member.summary:
Singleton service that owns the and instances for the lifetime of the DotnetClaw process.
Responsibilities: • Lazy-initialise Playwright and launch the configured browser on first use • Vend instances (persistent or fresh per request) • Dispose everything cleanly on shutdown
Persistent session mode ( = true): The same page is reused across calls — cookies, local storage, and login state survive between agent turns. The page is recreated if it's been closed.
Isolated session mode ( = false): A fresh page is created for every call to . The caller MUST dispose the session when finished.

member.name: P:DotnetClaw.Config.DotnetClawOptions.AllowedShellCommands
member.summary:
Allow-list of shell command prefixes. Only commands whose first token starts with one of these strings will be executed.
Empty list = developer mode (all commands allowed). In production or shared environments, always populate this list.
The block-list () is always checked first, regardless of this setting.
Example: ["dotnet", "git", "npm"]

member.name: P:DotnetClaw.Config.DotnetClawOptions.BlockedShellCommands
member.summary:
Block-list of shell command patterns. Commands matching any entry in this list are always rejected, even if they appear in .
Matching is done as a prefix check on the full command string (after trimming). Add patterns here for any command that must never be executed regardless of context.
Example: ["rm -rf /", "format", "del /f /s /q C:\\"]

member.name: T:DotnetClaw.Plugins.CursorPlugin
member.summary:
Cursor CLI skill — lets DotnetClaw invoke Cursor's headless coding agent (agent.exe / agent) as a sub-process.
Supported modes (maps to Cursor's --mode flag):
agent (default) — Cursor reads the codebase, plans, and applies edits autonomously. plan — Cursor produces a structured step-by-step plan, no file changes. ask — Cursor answers questions about the codebase, read-only.
CLI invocation format built by this plugin (matches cursor-agent CLI): agent -p --mode=agent "prompt" [--model ...] [--yes] --trust "<workspace>" [extraFlags] agent -p --mode=plan "prompt" [--model ...] --trust "<workspace>" [extraFlags] agent -p --mode=ask "prompt" [--model ...] --trust "<workspace>" [extraFlags]

member.name: T:DotnetClaw.Mcp.McpKernelLoader
member.summary:
Loads all connected MCP servers into the Semantic Kernel as named plugins.
Each MCP server becomes a plugin named Mcp_{serverName}. Every tool the server exposes becomes a inside that plugin — the agent can call them exactly like built-in skills.
Example — a "filesystem" MCP server with tools read_file, write_file, list_dir: Plugin "Mcp_filesystem" → KernelFunctions: read_file, write_file, list_dir
The bridge is powered by Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Plugins.MCP: IMcpClientExtensions.AsKernelPluginAsync(client, pluginName) converts MCP tool schemas → SK function metadata automatically.
